result.target_topic: Q1 2024 Goodwill Impairment for Intel Foundry
result.target_summary: Following a segment reporting modification in Q1 2024, Intel recognized a $222 million goodwill impairment loss for the Intel Foundry reporting unit, resulting in zero remaining goodwill for that unit. The impairment occurred because the fair value of the new reporting unit, which included substantially all allocated property, plant, and equipment, was lower than its carrying value.

comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose the results of their goodwill impairment assessments for fiscal year 2024, but with opposite outcomes. Intel recognized a $222 million goodwill impairment loss for its Intel Foundry reporting unit after a segment reorganization, resulting in zero remaining goodwill for that unit. In contrast, AMD conducted its annual qualitative impairment tests in the fourth quarter of 2024 and concluded that there was no goodwill impairment for any of its reporting units.

comparisons.peer_topic: Goodwill impairment testing methodology and frequency
comparisons.peer_summary: Goodwill is subject to an annual impairment test in the fourth fiscal quarter, or earlier if indicators exist, using either a qualitative or quantitative analysis on a reporting unit basis.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA (NVDA) disclose the timing and nature of their goodwill impairment testing processes. Intel performed quantitative impairment assessments immediately before and after its business reorganization in Q1 2024. Similarly, NVIDIA subjects goodwill to annual impairment tests during the fourth quarter, or earlier if indicators exist, utilizing either qualitative or quantitative analysis. Both companies utilize these tests to determine if goodwill on their reporting units is impaired.
